extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patentees, representatives, and counsel filing petitions before the IPTAB (Korean Ministry of Intellectual Property)
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural guidance for preparing and filing petitions for trials and appeals before Korea's Intellectual Property Trial and Appeal Board, covering petition submission, procedural steps, timelines, deadlines, withdrawal, publication of decisions, and permissible inquiries. Intended to explain how and when matters are processed and what rules govern filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to file a petition for a trial and/or appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: A written petition should be prepared and submitted to the President of IPTAB.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Once a written petition is filed, the proceeding is as follows: Formality Examination → Decision to Institute a Trial/Appeal (or if necessary, 'Issue an Order to Amend') → Hearing → Trial decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pendency / typical timeline
rubrics_metrics.description: Although pendency may vary depending on the type of trial or appeal, matters are generally decided on a first-come/first-served basis and take approximately 8 months on average from the date of filing of the petition until a trial decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IPTAB provides fast-track and accelerated trials for cases requiring an expedited decision, including trials with pending infringement lawsuits. IPTAB has set a target of issuing a decision within 3 months for fast-track trials and 6 months for accelerated trials from the date of filing a petition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability and publication of final decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Final decisions are available for search and download by visiting the KIPRIS website.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To prevent disclosure of personal information, documents go through a separate procedure to remove confidential information before publication; decisions will be available to the public approximately 1 month after the decision is rendered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deadline rules when last day falls on weekend or holiday
rubrics_metrics.description: If a deadline for filing a document to IPTAB falls on a weekend or holiday, Article 14(4) of the Patent Act applies: the period expires on the following working day.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: However, for the period for filing litigation for revocation of a trial decision or filing an appeal against the Board's decision, Article 14(4) does not apply. Instead, pursuant to Article 170 of the Civil Act in accordance with Article 8 of the Administration Litigation Act, Article 161 of the Civil Act applies: 'where the last day of a period falls on a Saturday or a national holiday, such period shall end on the following day.' Note that Labor Day may not be considered a 'Saturday or a national holiday' under Article 161, so the deadline may not shift in that case.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective date of document submission by mail vs court filings
rubrics_metrics.description: If a document is submitted to the IPTAB by mail, it is deemed filed on the date of the postmark stamped on the cover in which the document was mailed (Article 28(2) of the Patent Act).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documents submitted to the Patent Court or the Supreme Court, by contrast, are considered submitted on the actual date of receipt without exception.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal of petition
rubrics_metrics.description: A withdrawal of petition refers to withdrawing all or part of a proceeding. A request to withdraw may be filed before the decision is rendered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Once a written reply has been submitted by the opposite party (defendant), the defendant's consent is required to withdraw the petition according to Article 161(1) of the Patent Act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contact for procedural inquiries and limits on case-specific responses
rubrics_metrics.description: For inquiries regarding procedural matters of a case (such as submission of documents and evidence), contact MOIP's call center at 1544-8080 (currently only available in Korean).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Article 217 of the Patent Act prohibits giving expert opinion, testimony, or answers in response to an inquiry about a case for which a patent application, examination, trial, or retrial is pending with the IPTAB, or about the details of a decision or trial ruling on whether to grant or refuse a patent.
